discovery: Conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors, leading to the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson

nominees.name: Peter Jenni
nominees.affiliation: CERN and University of Freiburg, Germany

motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism, but the experimental discovery itself has not been recognised. The 2012 observation of a scalar boson near 125 GeV was possible only because of two general-purpose detectors of unprecedented granularity, radiation hardness and trigger capability, conceived in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Peter Jenni founded ATLAS and led it for fifteen years. Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee conceived CMS and led its design and construction. Their choices, including the toroidal and high-field solenoidal magnet concepts, precision calorimetry for H→γγ, and muon systems for H→ZZ*→4ℓ, made the discovery-level significance possible within three years of data-taking. Since then, Higgs couplings, the self-consistency of the Standard Model, and constraints on supersymmetry, dark matter and extended Higgs sectors have all come from these instruments. They were decisive individual contributions within a collective effort.
